chunks: Ibn Maskan said, and al-Hasan said: 'We heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:'

A foul-mouthed woman passed by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) while he was eating, and said, 'O Muhammad, you are indeed eating the food of a slave and sitting as a slave sits.' So he said to her, 'Woe to you! And who is a more submissive slave than me?' She said, 'Then give me a morsel of your food.' So the Messenger of Allah gave her a morsel of his food. She said, 'No, by Allah, unless you bring a morsel from your mouth to my mouth.' He said: 'So he took out the morsel from his mouth and gave it to her, and she ate it.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'She did not utter an obscene word until she left this world.'

key_terms.أَكْلَ الْعَبْدِ: The manner of eating of a slave (servant)
key_terms.بَذِّيَّةٌ: A woman known for foul speech or obscenity

ai.seo_question: What happened when a foul-mouthed woman asked the Prophet to feed her from his mouth?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the Prophet’s (SAW) humility and responsiveness to a specific challenge, illustrating the concept of *Bada'* or the transformative power of his physical presence. In Shia scholarly tradition, the act of transferring food directly from his mouth to hers symbolizes the transmission of spiritual purity (*Taharah*) and the removal of the 'filth' of her foul speech, validating the efficacy of the Prophet's tangible connection with his followers. The immediate cessation of her obscenity underscores the purifying nature of the Ahl al-Bayt's interaction with the world.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 22.Ibn Muskān said, and so did al-Ḥasan, “We heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (a) say,

‘A foul-mouthed woman once passed by the Messenger of Allah (ṣ) while he was eating, and said, ‘O Muḥammad, you are indeed eating the food of slaves sitting as a slave would sit.’ So he (ṣ) said to her, ‘Woe be to you! And who is a more submissive slave [of Allah] than me?’ She said, ‘Then share with me a morsel of your food.’ So the Messenger of Allah (ṣ) gave her some of his food. She said, ‘No, by Allah. I want a morsel from your mouth to [enter] my mouth!’ So he took out a morsel from his mouth and gave it to her, and she ate it.” Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) said,“After that, she never uttered an obscene word until she left this world.”
